subject.title: fix(memory-core): skip unchanged Dreaming workspace state writes

question: Should Memory Core accept that unchanged Dreaming rows no longer refresh keyed-store recency at the 50,000-row namespace cap, or must the optimization preserve the current refresh-based retention behavior?
rationale: The patch removes redundant synchronous SQLite writes but changes the only available recency signal used by keyed-store eviction; source and ordinary no-op proof cannot determine which retention policy maintainers intend for existing large workspaces.

options.title: Choose and test the retention contract
options.body: Document the intended capacity behavior, add a focused cap/eviction regression test, and merge the implementation that matches it.

options.title: Accept stable-row aging
options.body: Accept lower write pressure in exchange for unchanged rows aging toward eviction, with an explicit test proving that policy at capacity.

options.title: Preserve refresh semantics
options.body: Keep or add an owner-approved mechanism that refreshes recency without reserializing every unchanged value, then prove both no-op write reduction and eviction behavior.

recommendation.title: Choose and test the retention contract
recommendation.body: Document the intended capacity behavior, add a focused cap/eviction regression test, and merge the implementation that matches it.

likelyOwner.reason: A Memory Core/plugin-state owner must choose the persistent-state retention contract; the available context does not support naming an individual reliably.
